posts.name: Foote
posts.cooked:
The romance with OmniX people had (myself included in that company) fizzled as you played more games. I think the first time we all got hit with 5+ damage in a turn and lost 6+ components quashed those feelings swiftly.

Bunkers modes are really interesting and are quite good, but they require a "long view" vision. In todays microwave instant-gratification based world, Bunkers ideal playstyle butts heads with how we generally feel it should work. Take Chrono-Ranger as a perfect counter example. Everything is instant, in the moment, pew pew pew, profit. Bunker players, if you truely are interested in edging out as much out of him as possible, must be planning their play phases two turns in advanced. Upgrade Mode is a casualty of the instant-gratification mindset as its immediate benefits are few but the long term gains will pay for themselves in a few rounds. No wonder it is brought up so often when others talk about Bunker as a "low tier" hero. (It is the same mindset that prevents players from enjoying the Zen of Mr. Fixer in my opinion). 

Having said that, I think the new hero decks will appeal to many. Sentinels might (read: will) overtake Chrono as the insta-grata champs.

posts.name: phantaskippy
posts.cooked:
Recharge, Upgrade, Turret, all of his modes present opportunities with cost, when you play Recharge, you don't play cards till you destroy it.  When you switch out of recharge you are deciding to stop drawing huge amounts of cards so you can play/use powers.

You may hope to draw the cards you need for the desired set-up, but if you get some options but not all you want you have to make a choice of when to stop recharging and join the fight again.

Upgrade is often a tougher choice, esp. when you have a ton of good cards in hand.  Turret mode is awesome, but it essentially locks you down as long as it is on the field, you can't draw except with Ammo Drop and you can't play cards to improve your build.

Most people play Bunker looking to achieve a certain build, and while acheiving that build might hold a lot of value to the team, often players overlook higher leverage situations in trying to accomplish that build.

"Fixing what is in front of you" simply means you do whatever you can that turn to deal with the problems of that turn, if you can take an enemy out that would otherwise live and yet wait, you allow the situation to worsen.  Often the first few rounds of the game are where the game is actually settled, esp. villains that start with cards in play.  Taking a flyer on those rounds to do better later, when others tend to also be really powerful isn't worth it.

Take the shots you get, don't dump the early game on your team and work for end game, Bunker isn't built that way.

One of the reasons I like the house rule where you can return a mode to your hand to play another at the start of your turn is that rule allows players who really want Bunker to be more of a good early, strong end game hero to do just that.

For me, Bunker is a lot less about the end game, but how you get there. Sure, I think I know what you should play, but you don't always have the cards. The other day, I had a great game against Apostate in the Realm of Discord. Postivie Energy Field came out, so I went into Upgrade Mode with Bunker. With Bunker and Tachy playing two cards a round (plus the others), and no villain targets in play (destroyed the turn they came out), the heroes were gaining hp like crazy.

Once another distortion finally came out, Bunker had: Omni-Cannon, 2x Maintanence Unit, Heavy Plating, and Ammo Drop. Not a combo I would usually go to, but I dropped Turret Mode anyways. Bunker became the tank, gaining 4 hp a round, with 1 damage reduction. He would play Omni-Cannon every few rounds when he had the cards, and easily take out a relic and get by the damage reduction. 

I would probably never intentionally try that, but it just happened. There is so much about Bunker just playing what he has, and how he gets to his combo. Sometimes he gets it, sometimes he doesn't, but it's usually fun trying to get there.
